spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, save locations
description: Whole fixture machines (files, dirs, symlinks, core answers) in; the canonical contract serializations (atlas/contract.py) out, asserted with exact equality: installations (kind, kinds, root, health issue codes) and — per query — the full SavefilePlacement (dir, root_kind, needs, fallback_dir, physical_dir, file_set incl. completeness, granularity incl. option identity and alternatives, caveat codes + data), catalogue entries, and entry-route outcomes incl. Unresolved. Prose (sources, messages) is non-contractual. Layout facts are sourced from RetroArch runloop.c/configuration.c/config.def.h and the shipped RetroDECK/EmuDeck configs; see docs/research/retrodeck-save-placement.md.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-content-concrete
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK stock layout: cfg sets savefile_directory and sort-by-content. With a content path given, the placement is concrete: saves/<parent-dir-name>/. The existing save is observed, not guessed.

vectors.name: retrodeck-multi-disc-m3u-folder
vectors.rationale: The multi-disc convention: the ROM's parent directory is named '<title>.m3u'. content_dir is the parent directory name (runloop.c:8781), so the save lands under saves/<title>.m3u/ — observed on a real installation.

vectors.name: retrodeck-core-override-flips-sort
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK ships config/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg with sort_savefiles_by_content_enable=false — a stock installation where the core override flips the layout flat for PPSSPP-libretro. The override directory is keyed by library_name (PPSSPP), resolved live from the core binary.

vectors.name: retrodeck-game-override-wins-over-core-override
vectors.rationale: The chain stacks core → content-dir → game, later wins (configuration.c:7095). The core override turns sorting off; the game override turns it back on — the game override must win.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-core-resolves-library-name
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core appends library_name — the core's self-reported display name (mGBA), not the .so basename (mgba). Resolved live via query_core through the /app→Flatpak-deployment translation; the existing save is observed through it.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-core-without-core-leaves-hole
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core needs library_name; without a named core the hole stays open (a hole is not an unknown — the caller can fill it), and a caveat states that per-core overrides were not checked.

vectors.name: retrodeck-savefiles-in-content-dir
vectors.rationale: savefiles_in_content_dir: the save lives next to the ROM. With the content path given, the directory is the ROM's own folder, concrete.

vectors.name: retrodeck-root-missing-health
vectors.rationale: The commonest Steam Deck failure: retrodeck.json is readable but points at an unmounted SD card. Detection reports each folder the marker places on the card — the root, the saves root and the BIOS folder — as missing instead of handing out a syntactically correct path as if usable. The ROM root is not on the card here: without ES-DE settings it is the frontend's default on internal storage, which exists, so it states no finding.

vectors.name: retrodeck-no-query-detection-only
vectors.rationale: Detection without a placement question: retrodeck.json present, root exists, health ok.

vectors.name: emudeck-flat-layout
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck: settings.sh is the truth, the bare org.libretro.RetroArch Flatpak is its RetroArch, the shipped layout is flat (sort keys false). One handle for both descriptions — no separate bare installation.

vectors.name: standalone-flatpak-upstream-default-sorts-by-core
vectors.rationale: RetroArch's upstream compile-time default is sort_savefiles_enable=true (config.def.h:982). A bare Flatpak whose cfg sets only the directory sorts by core — the placement needs library_name.

vectors.name: standalone-flatpak-savefile-directory-absent
vectors.rationale: An unset savefile_directory means the RetroArch platform default — 'saves' under the config tree (platform_unix.c:2133-2134) — never the ROM's directory; upstream compile defaults then sort by core.

vectors.name: native-explicit-flat-with-observed-multifile-save
vectors.rationale: A native install with sorting explicitly off; the existing save is a core-written multi-file set (Beetle Saturn's .bcr/.bkr/.smpc). The file set is observed, never derived from an .srm assumption.

vectors.name: unloadable-core-is-stated-not-guessed
vectors.rationale: A core that is present but unloadable (missing host library — the applewin case) yields library_name unknown: the hole stays open and the caveat states it. Never a guess from the .so filename. This core carries no card, so nothing was retired and no core-generation-unestablished rides here — core-unqueryable already says the read failed, and a second caveat would announce the loss of knowledge that never existed.

vectors.name: a-core-no-interpreter-could-probe-states-that
vectors.rationale: The frozen-host case: nothing on this machine could run the probe, so no process was started and no core has a library_name. The hole and the caveat are the unloadable case's, and `reason` is what tells the two apart — a client that sees this on every core is looking at its own host rather than at a broken core, and the fix is to register an interpreter. That distinction is the whole point of the key: the message cannot carry it, because the seam and not the resolver is what observed it.

vectors.name: a-core-whose-probe-could-not-be-spawned-states-that
vectors.rationale: An interpreter was named here and starting it failed. Distinct from no-interpreter, because a caller acts differently: there the host registers one, here the one it registered does not run.

vectors.name: a-core-that-crashed-before-naming-itself-states-that
vectors.rationale: The probe died by signal before printing the line that names the core — the crash the subprocess exists to absorb, taken too early to have absorbed anything. A crash after that line is not this: the reading is the answer it already printed.

vectors.name: a-core-whose-probe-hung-states-that
vectors.rationale: The probe was killed at the timeout with nothing usable printed. The one empty reading a machine remembers, because a core that hangs once hangs again and the retry is the only one that costs the caller the whole timeout.

vectors.name: a-core-that-ran-and-named-itself-nothing-states-that
vectors.rationale: The probe ran to an end of its own and nothing it printed names a core: the core reported no library_name, or the output holds no line a reader can use at all. What was observed is the ending, not a diagnosis — the reading says the run finished by itself and named nothing, which is what separates it from a load the loader refused, from a crash, and from a hang.

vectors.name: symlinked-save-dir-reads-through
vectors.rationale: A save directory reached through a symlink (RetroDECK's dir_prep pattern): the fixture resolves link prefixes like the kernel, so the observed file set is found through the link.

vectors.name: coexistence-retrodeck-and-native
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations each get their own handle, RetroDECK first; no cross-installation fall-through and no silently chosen winner.

vectors.name: emudeck-claims-standalone-flatpak
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck is a configured org.libretro.RetroArch — the same RetroArch under two descriptions. One handle carrying both, never a second handle for the same installation.

vectors.name: emudeck-marker-paths-partially-quoted
vectors.rationale: What the app-driven installer actually writes: every path key quotes only its jq-read prefix (jsonToBashVars.sh:116-123 @ 863ab69) and source concatenates the segments into one word. The marker-derived root comes out quote-free and health does not false-alarm root-missing on a healthy machine — observed on a live EmuDeck installation.

vectors.name: nothing-installed
vectors.rationale: An empty machine detects nothing; an empty list is the truthful answer.

vectors.name: flycast-shared-vmus-in-system-directory
vectors.rationale: Flycast's default roots saves in system_directory, not savefile_directory: shared VMUs under <system_directory>/dc, one set for every game (rule card 'flycast', governing option reicast_per_content_vmus read live). Only the VMUs actually present are observed; granularity states the shared card and how to switch.

The id is written in the disc header, which atlas does not read: the file set is stated as the template it is and 'save_id' joins needs. Content without such an id — arcade, or a disc header stating none — is named after the ROM by the same function (oslib.cpp:62); atlas cannot decide which case it has, so 'filenames-content-conditional' carries both spellings, the alternative filled from the content path. A per-game VMU already lying in that directory is deliberately NOT attributed to this content — a content-sorted directory holds every game of one ROM directory, so reading a name back as this save would be a guess.

vectors.name: catalogue-declared-order-and-classification
vectors.rationale: The catalogue is read live from the bundled es_systems.xml in the Flatpak deployment: entries in declared order (first = ES-DE default), libretro entries carry their extracted core .so, standalone entries carry none.

vectors.name: catalogue-a-duplicate-label-is-dropped-and-takes-no-position
vectors.rationale: ES-DE stores a command only under `if (!duplicateLabel)` (SystemData.cpp:1067-1069 @ v3.4.1, the comparison at :1056-1066), so the second command bearing a label already kept never reaches mLaunchCommands. atlas states no entry for it either, and the command after it is declared_index 1 rather than 2 — numbering the elements would put every later entry a slot too high and name a different emulator than the frontend shows at that position.

vectors.name: catalogue-a-command-without-a-label-ends-the-walk
vectors.rationale: Once one command is kept, a <command> with no label attribute stops ES-DE's read of the system (SystemData.cpp:1031-1038 @ v3.4.1, 'only the first command tag will be processed'), and every later element goes with it. So a system declaring three commands answers with one entry at declared_index 0. The mirror image at :1048-1055 caps a system whose FIRST command carries no label at that single entry too, but that shape cannot be a vector: such an entry is kept under the empty label ES-DE reads from the absent attribute, and the corpus grammar refuses an empty emulator label (scripts/validate_vectors.py, 'emulator label must be a non-empty string'). It is covered by a direct-parser test instead (tests/test_esde.py::TestParse::test_a_labelless_first_command_makes_a_one_entry_system).

vectors.name: catalogue-custom-overlay-replaces-system
vectors.rationale: A system defined in the custom_systems overlay replaces the bundled system of the same name entirely (ES-DE USERGUIDE, Game System Customizations).

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-promotes-default
vectors.rationale: The user's saved per-system emulator choice lives in the gamelist.xml header as <alternativeEmulator><label> — written by ES-DE as two root elements (not well-formed XML, observed live). A matching label promotes that entry to effective default; the declared default stays as alternative.

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-inside-gamelist-promotes-default
vectors.rationale: The same saved choice, written where ES-DE is moving it: <alternativeEmulator> as a child of <gameList> instead of a second root element (ES-DE reads both, document level first — GamelistFileParser.cpp:190-192; the nested shape is what RetroDECK 0.10.9b carries live). Where the element sits must not change which emulator atlas calls the effective default.

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-of-the-declared-first-changes-no-order
vectors.rationale: The user's saved choice names the entry the layer already declared first, so promotion moves nothing: the order is the declared one and selection still says a user chose it. Read beside catalogue-gamelist-selection-promotes-default, where the promoted entry carries declared_index 1, this is what declared_index is for: entries[0] carries a selection in both answers, so selection alone cannot say whether the choice moved anything, and only the declared position tells the two apart.

vectors.name: lrps2-shared-memcards-through-symlink
vectors.rationale: LRPS2's default (pcsx2_shared_memory_cards=enabled, libretro_core_options.h:169) keeps shared memory cards under <system_directory>/pcsx2/memcards. Under RetroDECK that path is a dir_prep symlink into the saves tree; the observed card is found through the link. The option's 'disabled' mode switches to per-game <rom_stem>.ps2 in the save directory (verified in libretro/ps2 source).

vectors.name: retrodeck-cfg-missing-platform-default-applies
vectors.rationale: A RetroDECK whose retroarch.cfg is missing: RetroArch initializes platform defaults before config load (platform_unix.c:2133-2134), so the effective root is 'saves' under the config tree — never the ROM's directory — and the upstream compile defaults govern sorting (sort_savefiles_enable=true, config.def.h:982). The missing file is stated rather than left to this prose: health finds emulator-config-missing naming the cfg, and the same finding rides the save answer, which leaned on the defaults the file would have overridden.

vectors.name: retrodeck-cfg-unreadable-platform-default-applies
vectors.rationale: A RetroDECK whose retroarch.cfg exists and cannot be read: RetroArch's platform defaults stand in exactly as for a missing file, and the finding is config-unreadable with the path and the read status — the code a bare RetroArch states its own cfg with — on health and on the save answer that read the file.

vectors.name: entry-route-selection-to-placement
vectors.rationale: The natural client route: catalogue entry (with the gamelist selection applied) to its save placement in one ask. The promoted ParaLLEl entry resolves with its own core — the no-core caveat class does not exist on this path; the core is unaudited and the answer says so.

vectors.name: entry-route-standalone-is-unresolved
vectors.rationale: The entry route answers a standalone emulator atlas has no card for with a typed domain outcome rather than an exception — Ruffle here, a Flash player whose save behaviour nobody has read. RPCS3 held this example until its own VFS was read (#231), which is the point: the refusal is about evidence, not about the standalone kind.

vectors.name: entry-route-a-foreign-core-row-refuses-before-any-card
vectors.rationale: All four entry routes are asked of the row EmuDeck's n3ds overlay declares first, a RetroArch launch pointed at a Windows citra_libretro.dll, and all four refuse with core-file-foreign and the file's own name. The refusal is the point of the kind: the standalone dispatch these routes used to fall into looks the launch command's %EMULATOR_…% token up in the packaged cards, and the only token here is %EMULATOR_RETROARCH% — so a card found under it would answer with the trees of an emulator this row does not launch, and a card not found would say 'standalone emulator Citra is not resolvable yet' about an emulator that is not here at all. Neither is true, and the one code says what is: the entry hands RetroArch a core file this host cannot load, its name carrying another platform's suffix. Four routes and one word, where the standalone refusals are four words: what is missing there differs per family, and here nothing differs, because the launch runs RetroArch and RetroArch loads nothing, so no emulator of its own is running to have a tree of any family. The launchability answer is the same fact one question over: the system's accept-list declares .3ds on account of every row, the row that would run takes no file at all, and that split is exactly what entry-not-accepted says — with the sibling standalone row, whose own loader was read, named as the alternative.

vectors.name: emudeck-a-label-judges-the-sibling-it-names
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's n3ds overlay of entry-route-a-foreign-core-row-refuses-before-any-card, whose first row hands RetroArch a Windows core and takes no file at all. Asked with label 'Azahar (Standalone)', the question is about the standalone row a caller starts the game through: its own loader was read and takes .3ds, so the verdict is launchable with that row as the entry, and no alternatives, which only entry-not-accepted carries. The sealed bundled layer is stated as on the unlabelled answer.

vectors.name: a-sealed-emudeck-refuses-a-label-no-derived-entry-carries
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck with its bundled layer sealed and an overlay declaring nothing: gba is a system only the installed mGBA core declares, so launchability answers unknown on the sealed statement alone, with no entry judged. The launch command answers such a system from the entries derived from the cores and refuses a label none of them carries; launchability looks the label up in the same place and refuses it the same way, launch-command-label-unknown beside the sealed statement. A label the derived entry carries, mGBA, leaves the answer as it is without one.

vectors.name: secondary-handle-answers-its-own-config
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations: the query names the native handle explicitly, and the answer comes from the native cfg alone — no cross-installation fall-through from the higher-priority RetroDECK.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-unreadable-is-present-and-broken
vectors.rationale: An unreadable marker is a PRESENT, broken RetroDECK — detection triggers on existence, and health separates the read failure from the root fallout instead of hiding the installation.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-invalid-json
vectors.rationale: Malformed JSON is not the same as an empty config object: the marker parses to nothing, health says marker-invalid, and the path fallbacks still answer.

vectors.name: a-roms-path-atlas-no-longer-reads-cannot-make-the-marker-invalid
vectors.rationale: roms_path is type-checked nowhere any more, because nothing reads it: the ROM root comes off ES-DE's own ROMDirectory, and retrodeck.json's copy is only the value RetroDECK seds into that setting. The scoping rule is that atlas reports on what it reads, so a key no read touches cannot make an installation unhealthy — reporting it would be a claim about who wrote the file. This machine is healthy with a roms_path that is not even a string, which is exactly the answer a marker-invalid finding here would get wrong.

vectors.name: sorted-dir-blocked-by-file-reverts-to-root
vectors.rationale: A file where the sorted directory belongs: RetroArch's mkdir MUST fail and it reverts to the unsorted root (runloop.c:8844) — the fallback is not conditional, it is the known answer.

vectors.name: lrps2-dead-memcard-link-is-stated
vectors.rationale: The dir_prep link into an unmounted volume: the emulator-side memcards path is dead. The answer keeps the emulator-side directory and states the dead link with its target — physical_dir stays null because there is no existing backing path.

vectors.name: lrps2-memcard-link-cycle-is-stated
vectors.rationale: The other way a dir_prep link ends nowhere: the chain closes on itself, so the kernel answers ELOOP for the whole resolution rather than reaching any path at all. It is its own code next to dead-symlink because the two need different repairs — a dead link points at a name somebody can create, a cycle is one somebody has to break — and a consumer that branches only on dead-symlink to find an unwritable directory must miss this one. physical_dir stays null: there is no backing path, not even a half-resolved one to name.

vectors.name: emudeck-stale-marker-companion-missing
vectors.rationale: settings.sh survives while the claimed org.libretro.RetroArch Flatpak is gone: the EmuDeck handle stays (it claims the bare identity), and its health exposes the missing companion config instead of silently suppressing a bare handle.

vectors.name: opera-nvram-subdir-unanswered-when-no-mode-is-established
vectors.rationale: 3DO NVRAM (rule card 'opera') on a core the probe could not read: it loaded and answered, but registered no options this probe captured, so it declared a default for neither switch the card's rule reads. The card records neither either — a default is written down only for a core that registers none, and this one normally does. With no options file on the machine nothing states the storage or the version, so the rule cannot name one of the twenty modes and steps aside rather than nesting a subdirectory on the strength of nothing. One core-option-value-unestablished per unread switch says which; the version comparison still runs and still reports that this card was never verified on any arrangement. Read the core's registration on this same machine and it answers mode per-game-0 in saves/opera/per_game, observing the 'Road Rash (USA).0.srm' it already carries — an observed set with no groups, which is a different answer from the declared one a machine without that file gives.

vectors.name: opera-card-retires-when-the-core-registers-one-of-its-two-switches
vectors.rationale: The same 3DO machine with a core that registers opera_nvram_storage and not opera_nvram_version. A rule card declares every option its rule reads, and feature detection is the plural of the single-option check: one missing switch means the rule would be reading something this core does not have, so the card retires as a generation mismatch naming the switch it could not find. The stale per_game file on disk is left where it is — the card is not applied, so nothing observes under its names. This machine used to answer with the subdirectory, back when the card read the storage switch alone.

vectors.name: opera-shared-nvram-unanswered-when-only-the-storage-switch-is-read
vectors.rationale: The options file states opera_nvram_storage = shared and the probe captured no core options, so the version switch is stated nowhere. Half a reading is not a mode: the file name carries the version, so the rule refuses rather than naming opera/shared on the strength of the switch it did read. Exactly one core-option-value-unestablished rides, and it names the version — the switch that was read is not reported as missing.

vectors.name: opera-per-game-nvram-named-from-the-cores-own-defaults
vectors.rationale: The shipped Opera binary as the probe really reads it: both save switches registered, opera_nvram_storage defaulting to 'per game' and opera_nvram_version to '0'. No options file states either, so those live defaults govern — machine facts, not recorded ones — and the rule names mode per-game-0. vectors.name: override-switches-the-game-opt-layer-off

There is nothing to fall back to, so the card steps aside with core-option-value-unestablished instead of reporting an unknown-option-value it could recover from. vectors.rationale: EmuDeck deploys upstream ES-DE as an AppImage and wires it through plain files under ~/ES-DE (dragoonDorise/EmuDeck @ 863ab69; ES-DE v3.4.1). The catalogue answers come from the readable layers — the custom_systems overlay EmuDeck writes, the gamelist selections it seeds, es_settings.xml's ROMDirectory — and every one carries emulator-catalogue-sealed, because the bundled es_systems.xml is embedded in the AppImage (INSTALL.md v3.4.1:1470) and atlas does not open it. An overlay system answers fully (ES-DE's merge replaces a same-name bundled system entirely), the gamelist's alternativeEmulator promotes Virtual Jaguar over the declared order, and %ROMPATH% resolves against the ROMDirectory EmuDeck itself wrote (emuDeckESDE.sh:407-409).

The answer never reads as 'the frontend knows no emulator for gb' — since issue #133 it carries the DERIVED enumeration instead: the installed cores' own systemname files them under the asked id, stated as emulator-list-derived beside the sealed statement. This fixture installs no cores, so the derived list is empty too — and still marked derived, never 'declares none'. Same for the ROM placement: no rom-path-undeclared, because the declaration may sit in the sealed layer.

vectors.name: emudeck-esde-on-disk-outranks-a-marker-that-says-no

vectors.name: emudeck-marker-promises-an-esde-the-disk-does-not-have

The disk decides; the record is stated, never followed.

vectors.name: emudeck-esde-ignores-a-portable-txt-beside-the-appimage
vectors.rationale: A portable.txt next to the AppImage moves nothing: an AppImage ES-DE looks for portable.txt in getExePath() (main.cpp:148-149 at v3.4.1), the directory of the canonical /proc/self/exe (FileSystemUtil.cpp:383-404) — inside the image's own mount, never the folder the image file sits in. With an empty one beside the 3.4.1 AppImage, --version prints no "Found portable.txt" line, though the check runs before --version is handled (main.cpp:148-154 against :398). So nothing about the file is stated, and the home-derived ROMDirectory default resolves against the user's home (~/ROMs, FileData.cpp:283-284), exactly as on the machine without the file — a directory this machine does not have, which health states as roms-root-missing. The enumeration is what the on-disk tree declares, with the sealed statement for the layer inside the AppImage.

vectors.name: emudeck-entry-route-beside-a-portable-txt-states-no-relocation

The direct question on the same machine is the contrast, and the reason this vector asks it too: same content, same core, the same placement and the same two core caveats, and no sealed statement — the direct route reads no ES-DE. vectors.name: emudeck-the-appimage-embedded-catalogue-unseals
vectors.rationale: The bundled es_systems.xml lives inside the AppImage's zstd squashfs, and a runtime that can open it reads the bundled layer itself (issue #65): the catalogue is complete, nothing is sealed, no list is derived — and an embedded system's own <platform> tag is read live, like any declared system's.

vectors.name: emudeck-a-runtime-without-the-codec-keeps-the-seal
vectors.rationale: The capability is the runtime's, not the machine's: where the interpreter lacks the image's codec (compression.zstd arrives with Python 3.14), the bundled layer stays exactly what it always was — sealed, stated, and never guessed at.

vectors.name: retrodeck-deployed-without-its-marker-is-not-set-up
vectors.rationale: The RetroDECK Flatpak is deployed in the system installation and retrodeck.json is not there: RetroDECK writes that marker at the start of its first launch, and its first-run setup deletes it again when left at the storage step, so it has not been started for this home or left that setup there. That is an installation, and its one health finding is not-set-up — no root-missing or saves-root-missing beside it, because those roots are paths setup has not created yet. Every other question refuses with the finding: the catalogue the deploy ships declares gba, and still no system, entry, ROM directory, save directory or firmware root is named, because what RetroDECK's setup writes decides them.

vectors.name: retrodeck-deployed-for-the-user-without-its-marker-is-not-set-up
vectors.rationale: The same state under the user installation, which flatpak searches first: a deploy there is the one that runs, and with no retrodeck.json it is not-set-up the same way. The systems question, a savestate and the firmware inventory each refuse with the finding.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-states-a-missing-bios-folder
vectors.rationale: The BIOS folder is checked the way the saves root is: retrodeck.json's bios_path names a folder on a card that is not mounted while the root and the saves root are present, and health states bios-root-missing with that path instead of reporting the installation healthy. bios_path is RetroDECK's own value, not RetroArch's system_directory, so the finding stands on the marker alone.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-states-a-missing-default-rom-root
vectors.rationale: No ES-DE settings file is a reading, not a refusal: the frontend falls back on <home>/ROMs, its home being the Flatpak config directory the launcher passes as --home, and that default is the ROM root health checks. It is not there, so health states roms-root-missing with the default's path.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-finds-the-default-rom-root-present
vectors.rationale: The same machine with the frontend's default ROM root in place: the root, the saves root, the BIOS folder and the ROM root are all directories, so health states nothing.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-states-a-missing-configured-rom-root
vectors.rationale: ES-DE's ROMDirectory points at a card that is not mounted while the default <home>/ROMs exists: the configured value is the root the frontend launches from, so it is the one checked, and health states roms-root-missing with its path.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-checks-the-rom-root-after-the-frontends-tilde-expansion
vectors.rationale: A ROMDirectory with ~ is expanded the way the frontend expands it, against its own home (the Flatpak config directory), and the expanded path is what health checks and names.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-states-es-de-settings-that-do-not-parse
vectors.rationale: ES-DE's settings file reads as text and does not parse, so the ROM root it sets is unknown: health states config-unreadable with the file and the status unparseable, the same status the ROM-location answer carries, rather than checking the default a file that sets something has no claim to.

vectors.name: retrodeck-health-states-each-missing-folder-beside-a-missing-root
vectors.rationale: An unmounted card holding the whole tree: the root, the saves root, the BIOS folder and the configured ROM root are each checked on their own, and a missing root suppresses none of the others.

vectors.name: emudeck-health-states-a-missing-bios-folder
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's biosPath names a folder on a card that is not mounted while the Emulation tree, the saves root and ES-DE's ROM root are present: health states bios-root-missing with that path.

vectors.name: emudeck-health-states-a-missing-rom-root
vectors.rationale: ES-DE is on this EmuDeck and its ROMDirectory points at a card that is not mounted: the ROM root is what roms_dir() answers, and health states roms-root-missing with it.

vectors.name: emudeck-health-states-es-de-settings-it-could-not-read
vectors.rationale: ES-DE is on this EmuDeck and its settings file is there with bytes that cannot be read, so the ROM root it sets is unknown: health states config-unreadable with the file and the read status, rather than checking the default ES-DE uses only where nothing is set.

vectors.name: emudeck-health-states-a-relative-romdirectory
vectors.rationale: ES-DE is on this EmuDeck and its ROMDirectory is relative even after the frontend's ~ expansion, so there is no ROM root to check: health states roms-root-not-absolute with the value as the file spells it.

vectors.name: emudeck-health-finds-both-folders-present
vectors.rationale: ES-DE's ROM root and EmuDeck's BIOS folder are both directories, so health states nothing about either.

vectors.name: emudeck-health-without-es-de-checks-the-bios-folder-only
vectors.rationale: No ES-DE on this EmuDeck (no AppImage, no ~/ES-DE tree), so there is no frontend ROM root and no ROM finding is stated, though ES-DE's default ~/ROMs does not exist either. The BIOS folder is still checked, and is missing.

vectors.name: retrodeck-an-appended-config-moves-the-save-directory
vectors.rationale: A launch that appends its own cfg (--appendconfig) moves the save directory: RetroArch merges the appended file into the global cfg before any override (configuration.c:6309-6353), so its savefile_directory and sort flag stand. The file sits in the home directory the RetroDECK sandbox is granted, so its visibility is established and no note rides.

The cards are in this folder all the same: every card the core opens is a name joined onto it (pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:2110-2113, the folder at :2337).

vectors.name: pcee2-a-standalone-pcsx2-ini-leaves-the-card-names-unstated
vectors.rationale: A standalone PCSX2.ini stands under <system>/pcsx2/inis, and the core adopts its [MemoryCards] section before it reads its own options (Libretro.cpp:562-596 at 340ce04): its names can stand in for the slots' and its multitap entries can add cards. atlas does not read them, so the answer names the card folder with files null and file-names-unestablished (#664 D9).

data.citation: A standalone PCSX2.ini stands under <system>/pcsx2/inis, or may stand there where atlas cannot tell, and the core adopts its [MemoryCards] section before it reads its own options (pcee2-libretro/Libretro.cpp:562-596, ReadCoreOptions after it at :2093, both at 340ce04): with no card in the folder its slot file names name the cards the core creates, and its multitap entries add cards beside them. atlas does not read those names, so the folder is stated and the names are not.

vectors.name: lrps2-shared-cards-through-the-link-are-pcee2s-too
vectors.rationale: LRPS2 in its default shared mode keeps its memory cards under <system>/pcsx2/memcards (DataRoot at libretro/main.cpp:1909-1913, memcards at pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:1043 and :1062 at 14d19f8), and PCEE2 composes the same folder itself (pcee2-libretro Libretro.cpp:481-487, pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:2311 and :2337 at 340ce04). Under RetroDECK that folder is a link into the saves tree. PCEE2 is installed and its own save answer for this content names the same folder after the link is resolved, so LRPS2's answer carries save-files-shared-with-core naming pcee2, with the link's target as dir — the mirror of PCEE2's caveat (#664 D6, D10).

vectors.name: lrps2-without-the-link-the-folder-is-still-pcee2s
vectors.rationale: LRPS2 in its default shared mode keeps its memory cards under <system>/pcsx2/memcards (DataRoot at libretro/main.cpp:1909-1913, memcards at pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:1043 and :1062 at 14d19f8), and PCEE2 composes the same folder itself (pcee2-libretro Libretro.cpp:481-487, pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:2311 and :2337 at 340ce04). Here the folder is a plain directory rather than RetroDECK's link; both answers name it all the same, so save-files-shared-with-core names pcee2 with that folder as dir.

PCEE2 is not installed on this machine, so it has no save answer to compare and nothing writes the folder beside LRPS2: no save-files-shared-with-core is stated.

vectors.name: lrps2-in-per-game-mode-shares-no-folder
vectors.rationale: pcsx2_shared_memory_cards is disabled, so LRPS2 writes a per-game card into RetroArch's save folder (libretro/main.cpp:1998-2010 at 14d19f8) and its answer never names <system>/pcsx2/memcards. PCEE2 still writes that folder, but not LRPS2's for this game, so no save-files-shared-with-core is stated (#664 D10).

vectors.name: lrps2-pcee2-with-both-slots-off-shares-no-folder
vectors.rationale: LRPS2 in its default shared mode keeps its memory cards under <system>/pcsx2/memcards (DataRoot at libretro/main.cpp:1909-1913, memcards at pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:1043 and :1062 at 14d19f8), and PCEE2 composes the same folder itself (pcee2-libretro Libretro.cpp:481-487, pcsx2/Pcsx2Config.cpp:2311 and :2337 at 340ce04).
